solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: Really enjoy being into solvent briefly, having an easy time

indicators.note: something being into another is placed inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: solvent means in credit, abbreviated as IN CR
to really enjoy something is to love it

explanation.surface: Someone who is comfortably in the black can relax and have an easy life.
explanation.walkthrough: Solvent means in credit, and the abbreviation IN CR opens to take the love.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in clover is an idiom for living comfortably and prosperously, without worries.

clue.text: What Brown represents: a new Balfour? F-off!

indicators.note: off means removed, so the named letter is taken away from the surname
a new version of the name is a remade one, with its letters reorganised

blocks.note: taken as written: Arthur Balfour, Conservative prime minister
the letter itself, to be dropped

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal of the idea that Gordon Brown is just a modern version of the Tory Balfour.
explanation.walkthrough: Gordon Brown was the Labour prime minister in 2008; 'F-off' doubles as a rude retort and an instruction to lose the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Gordon Brown led the Labour Party, so Labour is the party he stood for as prime minister.

clue.text: Can, crushed and stuffed in old bloke having depression

indicators.note: a crushed tin is bent out of shape, so its letters are mangled into a new order
stuffed in means pushed inside, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: cove is old slang for a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: A crushed can is jammed into an old fellow who is feeling low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' suggests the bloke's mood, but it is a hollow in a surface. Cove is dated British slang for a chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A concave surface curves inward, so it has a hollow or dip in it.

clue.text: (+ 22ac.) Fag's boxers possibly getting stiff

blocks.note: boxers are one breed of dog, hence 'possibly'
a stiff is slang for a dead body

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about a young man's underpants getting stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: At British public schools a fag was a junior boy who ran errands for a senior; boxers are the dogs, not the shorts.
explanation.definitionFit: A fag in the public-school sense is a junior servant doing menial chores, exactly what a dogsbody is.

clue.text: Girl, fancy car, top off, bloke getting end away

indicators.note: with its top off a down word loses its first letter
getting the end away means the final letter is sent off

blocks.note: a limousine, the fancy car, shortened to limo
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A girl, a flash car, a topless scene and a bloke having his end away: a sordid tabloid tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting his end away' is British slang for having sex; here it just means the last letter goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Imogen is a girl's name, best known from Shakespeare's Cymbeline.

clue.text: Flood survivor's lack of expression of sexual satisfaction?

blocks.note: no expresses an absence
a contented sigh

explanation.surface: A joke that the man on the ark never got to sigh with pleasure.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Noah built the ark and outlived the great Flood with his family and the animals.

clue.text: Mostly worried about nothing following business procedure to divert motions

indicators.note: worried means fretted or shaken about, so the letters of the first word are tossed into a new order
about means going round, so the shuffled word wraps around the next piece
following tells you the preceding pieces come after the company abbreviation

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
taken as written
zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone mostly worried about nothing after a business deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' pretends to qualify 'worried' but is the anagram fodder in full; 'motions' are bowel movements, not proposals.
explanation.definitionFit: A colostomy is surgery that reroutes the colon to an opening in the abdomen, diverting faeces.

clue.text: Sting roping in Brown and, later, Cyclops to mount a hit

indicators.note: roping in means lassoing and pulling inside, so the other pieces are taken within
in a down clue, mounting means climbing upward, so the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: a sting hurts
Gordon Brown was Prime Minister
the setter, Cyclops, refers to himself as I

explanation.surface: The singer Sting recruits Gordon Brown and the setter to climb aboard a hit record.
explanation.walkthrough: Sting is not the singer but a sharp pain; the PM goes in after the first letter of the pain and the setter later, after the second.
explanation.definitionFit: A hit is a great success, and a triumph is the same: a notable victory or achievement.

clue.text: Celebrity parasite supporter of capital punishment? No, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so the two letters come out in a different order

blocks.note: someone in favour of hanging
taken as written

explanation.surface: A star's leech asked whether they back the death penalty, and they answer no.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hanger' also reads as a clothes hanger, but here it is someone keen on the noose.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a sycophantic follower who attaches themself to someone famous for the reflected benefits.

clue.text: see 16dn.
One-on-one at work leads to bad character

blocks.note: one as the Roman numeral I, placed on one as the article A
something that is go is working, in operation

explanation.surface: A one-to-one meeting at the office leads to trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Iago is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello, a famously wicked dramatic role.

clue.text: see 23ac.
Gnome TV broadcast includes Brenda and new Labour ministers

indicators.note: broadcast also means scattered widely, like seed, so the letters are strewn into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Lord Gnome's TV channel features the Queen and the New Labour cabinet.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord Gnome is Private Eye's fictional proprietor; 'new Labour' looks like one phrase but 'new' is a letter of fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: In 2008 Labour held power, so its ministers made up the government of the day.

clue.text: Burst into laughter when Conservatives' leader goes "Accumulated points"

indicators.note: the leader of a group is the one at the front, so its opening letter is kept
goes means departs, so that letter leaves the phrase

blocks.note: to crack up is to burst out laughing
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: Everyone laughed when the Tory leader boasted about the points he had scored.
explanation.definitionFit: To rack up points is an idiom for accumulating them, as a score builds during a game.

clue.text: Flipping bollocks about rock group "Tingle"

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the word is read back to front
about means surrounding, so the turned word goes round the band

blocks.note: bollocks and rot both mean nonsense
R.E.M. is the American rock band

explanation.surface: An exasperated dismissal of a rock band's song called 'Tingle'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British swearword, but it is the signal to turn the nonsense round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremor is a slight quiver or shiver, close to the thrill of a tingle.

clue.text: (& 10ac.) Prick's excuses for Westminster perks?

blocks.note: member is a euphemism for prick, with the possessive
to make allowances is to excuse

explanation.surface: A sneer at some MP's lame justifications for his perks at Westminster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prick' looks like an insult for the MP; it is the vulgar sense, giving a word that also means an MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Members' allowances are the expenses paid to MPs at Westminster, a scandal-prone perk of office.

clue.text: The old guard talk affectionately before and partly during post-menopausal treatment

indicators.note: before tells you this part of the cooing goes at the front
partly during means a portion of the word sits inside the next piece

blocks.note: to coo is to murmur fondly
hormone replacement therapy

explanation.surface: Elderly ladies cooing over each other while on hormone therapy.
explanation.walkthrough: The coo is split: two letters stand in front and the last goes inside the hormone therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cohort was a division of a Roman legion, a body of soldiers in the ancient army.

clue.text: US conservative types and what they hate: strangling pet

indicators.note: strangling means gripping round the throat, so one word wraps around the other

blocks.note: reds are communists, loathed by the US right
to pet and to neck both mean to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: American right-wingers throttling the very things they despise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun, a household animal, but it is the verb for smooching.
explanation.definitionFit: Redneck is a derogatory US term for a rural, working-class white conservative.

clue.text: Bollocking wet in Bristol to an Aussie, Warren

indicators.note: a bollocking is a severe telling-off that shakes you up, so the letters are thrown about
in means placed inside, so the jumbled word goes within the slang term

blocks.note: a bristol is a breast in rhyming slang, and an Australian calls one a nork
taken as written

explanation.surface: An Australian called Warren gets a fierce telling-off for being wet in Bristol.
explanation.walkthrough: Bristols is British rhyming slang for breasts (Bristol City, titty); Warren looks like a man's name but is the rabbit burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: A warren is a maze of interconnecting tunnels or passages, so a network of them.

clue.text: Woman standing by bloke (died the day before) – credit to Londoners?

blocks.note: a woman's name
a bloke is a man
D is the abbreviation for died
the eve is the day before an event

explanation.surface: A woman stays loyal to her man who died the previous day, a tribute Londoners respect.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney rhyming slang: Adam and Eve means believe, so 'credit' is the verb, not money.
explanation.definitionFit: To credit something is to believe it, and in Cockney rhyming slang Adam and Eve stands for believe.

clue.text: Tossers whose output is frozen?

blocks.note: surface reading: idiots, whose efforts come to nothing
setter's reading: men who masturbate to supply sperm banks, where the sample is stored frozen

explanation.walkthrough: Tosser is British slang for an idiot and literally a masturbator; the question mark flags the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Sperm donors give samples that clinics freeze and store for later fertility treatment.

clue.text: see 4dn.
Di going spare, kicked it, Di kicked it

definitions.note: what Di kicked, in 'kicked the bucket'

indicators.note: going spare means surplus and so thrown out, leaving those letters behind

blocks.note: a horse that bucked kicked out
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mocking line about Princess Diana losing her temper and then dying.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the D and I from the middle of the kicking phrase leaves the answer; Diana, who died, kicked the bucket, so it is what she kicked.
explanation.definitionFit: To kick the bucket is an idiom for dying, so a bucket is the thing someone who died is said to have kicked.

clue.text: (& 12ac.) Glance from performing topless sex partner captivating civil engineer

indicators.note: topless means with the top removed, so the opening letter goes
captivating means holding captive, so the pair of pieces holds the engineer between them

blocks.note: an actor performing is on stage
a lover is a sexual partner
CE is the abbreviation for civil engineer

explanation.surface: A topless performer's lover gives a civil engineer the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: A once-over is a quick look or inspection, so a glance.

clue.text: He's often mounted Brenda after Daisy and drink

indicators.note: after means the Queen's letters come behind the animal and the drink

blocks.note: Daisy is a stock name for a cow
punch is a mixed drink
Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: A smutty suggestion that someone regularly mounts the Queen after a drink and a woman called Daisy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' is the cowboy on horseback, not the innuendo.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowpuncher is a cowboy, who spends much of his working day on horseback.

clue.text: Cocaine dose for Bill

blocks.note: C is slang for cocaine
a hit is a dose of a drug

explanation.surface: A line of coke on the tab for a man called Bill.
explanation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a name; it is an invoice.
explanation.definitionFit: A chit is a note recording a sum owed, such as a bar or restaurant bill.

clue.text: British plonker, that is, an alternative to Ray, bust in here

definitions.note: cryptic: the garment that holds a bust

blocks.note: BR is the abbreviation for British
a plonker is a fool, an ass
i.e., the Latin abbreviation for that is
the second note of the sol-fa scale is spelt either ray or re

explanation.surface: A British fool, a stand-in for someone called Ray, is caught breaking in.
explanation.walkthrough: Plonker is British slang for an idiot; 'bust' reads as breaking in, but it is a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A brassiere is a bra, the undergarment that contains and supports a woman's breasts.

clue.text: County ditching small idiot

indicators.note: ditching means dumping, so the named letter is thrown away

blocks.note: Berks is the abbreviation for Berkshire, an English county
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: A county council throws out an insignificant fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Berk is British slang for a fool, from the rhyming slang Berkshire Hunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A berk is a stupid person, a mild British insult synonymous with a twit.
